summary: TLS renegotiation at regional egress causing streaming stalls and elevated p99 in us-west
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 01:40 UTC we have observed a region-scoped spike in streaming stalls and request timeouts from customers in us-west. Symptoms indicate prolonged TLS handshake durations and repeated TLS renegotiation events at the regional egress population, which correlates with p95/p99 token latency increases and streaming disconnects for long-running connections.

Impact: Affected dedicated customers (example: NimbleAI) reported elevated p95/p99 generation latency (baseline p99 ~900ms token -> observed p99 ~2.6s) and intermittent streaming cancellations. Some API calls returned 5xx after client-side streaming timeout. Approx 8% of streams in us-west experienced at least one stall or disconnect during the window.

Environment: production; us-west egress POP (edge-eu-west-style naming: egress-usw-3). Affected inbound paths primarily via api-us-west.redwood.run -> regional egress proxy -> serving-runtime. No code rollout coincident with spike.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate a streaming chat session (stream=true) using redwood-7b-v1 pinned in us-west. 2) Send a prompt that produces multi-chunk responses (~1500 tokens). 3) Observe streaming frames: stalls appear between frame boundaries; some streams reset with TLS errors. Intermittent; higher probability during peak traffic windows.

Observed behavior: TLS handshake durations (full handshake) at p99 observed 700ms-1400ms in egress logs. NGINX-style egress proxy logs show repeated TLS renegotiation markers and TLS session ticket misses. Packet captures (pcap) show client re-initiating handshake mid-stream for new subconnections.

Expected behavior: Long-lived streaming sessions should reuse TLS sessions/tickets and avoid full handshakes on new frames or connection re-use; p99 token latency should stay within SLA targets.

Logs and traces: - egress-proxy access logs: increased "TLS_RENEG" annotations between 2026-03-10 01:40 and 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC. - X-Request-Id traces link: 8a7f-... show handshake->delay->stream-cancel pattern. - tcpdump excerpt and TLS handshake timing attached in attachments.

Workaround applied: SRE temporarily increased keepalive and allowed longer session ticket lifetime on egress proxies; this reduced immediate failures but did not fully eliminate p99 spikes. Temporary traffic steering of high-volume customers to another us-west POP mitigated impact for NimbleAI.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer reported widespread streaming stalls from us-west. Collected traces and asked SRE to triage. Logged in #support and opened this ticket.

2026-03-10 02:22 UTC — SRE (Diego): Noted large number of TLS session ticket misses and increased process CPU on egress proxies. Suspect session cache pressure or buggy session ticket keys. Spinning up additional egress proxies for immediate capacity relief.

2026-03-10 03:10 UTC — SRE (Diego): After rolling extra proxies, incidents decreased but p99 remained elevated. Packet capture demonstrates renegotiation requests coming from our egress process toward upstream TLS stacks (unexpected). Opened infra PR to collect more detailed SSL stats (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-10 04:15 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed partial improvement after traffic steering. Asked for ETA on root cause.

2026-03-11 09:40 UTC — Network Vendor (CDN team): Confirmed a recent config change in regional edge (auto-rotate session-ticket keys) that can trigger session reuse failures if rotation is faster than ticket lifetime. Coordinating to revert/adjust rotation cadence for us-west.

2026-03-12 14:02 UTC — SRE (Diego): Rolled hotfix to egress proxies to add defensive behavior: treat missing ticket as cache miss without triggering renegotiation; also lengthened session-ticket lifetime. Monitoring for 24h.

2026-03-13 08:30 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer NimbleAI reports latencies back to baseline and no streaming disconnects in last 12h. Closing customer-impacting loop; keeping ticket open for follow-ups.
2026-03-13 12:05 UTC — SRE (Diego): Post-mortem draft created; recommending follow-ups in infra backlog.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between elevated CPU on egress proxy workers and frequency of TLS_FULL_HANDSHAKE events in logs.

Packet captures show the egress proxy initiating or requesting TLS renegotiation when receiving certain upstream ACK patterns; hypothesis: session-ticket rotation race causing proxy to not find valid ticket and force full handshake.
Replayed traffic in staging with accelerated ticket rotation and reproduced p99 handshake spikes and stream stalls.
Histogram of handshake durations showed bimodal distribution: fast reuses (<50ms) and full handshakes (700-1400ms). The latter matches user-observed stalls.
Confirmed CDN/edge vendor had a config push to auto-rotate session-ticket keys in us-west on 2026-03-09 23:58 UTC. Reverting rotation cadence reduces full handshakes in test window.
Checked serving-runtime metrics: KV cache and inference kernels unaffected; root cause isolated to TLS session layer at egress.
Linked internal INT-441: previous ticket with session-ticket expiry bug in proxy library (older version) — investigating whether same code path was reintroduced in recent infra upgrade.
Collecting flamegraphs for egress proxy worker CPU to ensure no additional hot paths exist post-fix.
resolution:
Immediate: Increased TLS session-ticket lifetime and adjusted egress proxies to avoid triggering renegotiation on ticket miss. Reverted aggressive session-ticket rotation on regional CDN. Customer traffic steering reduced customer impact during mitigation.

Longer-term actions: 1) Patch egress proxy library to handle ticket rotation race (PR referenced). 2) Add integration test to simulate ticket rotation and verify streaming behavior. 3) Add alert for TLS_FULL_HANDSHAKE_rate > baseline and dashboard widget for handshake duration distribution per pop. 4) Run canary of rotated ticket config with health checks.

Status: Customer-visible issues resolved as of 2026-03-13. Engineering follow-ups logged and assigned to infra backlog (INT-441 reference).
